A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same implicit-reasoning scaling study, with readable main text and appendices. Methods, equations, original experiments, tables and code can be matched reliably despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: V2 reports original language-model experiments on FB15K-237 and synthetic knowledge graphs, graph-generation ablations, and an empirical scaling-law fit.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds sentence-based experiments and analyses comparing synthetic and real graph structure.

M1.justification: The Llama pretraining objective, completion procedure and synthetic graph-generation algorithm remain unchanged. The graph-generation code matches across v2 Appendix B and v3 Appendix D after accounting for formatting.

E1.justification: Section 3 adds GPT4-generated and templated sentence scenarios alongside random-ID triples, introducing lexical and syntactic input variation. The underlying FB15K-237 facts, synthetic graphs and knowledge-completion task remain.

E2.justification: Both versions compare Llama model-size variants without adding external reasoning baselines. GPT4 generates training sentences in v3; it is not evaluated as a competing reasoning model.

E3.justification: The added sentence experiments introduce GPT4/template conversion and different model/step grids, approximately 20–1287M parameters and up to 15,620 steps. GPT-generated text uses a pretrained tokenizer. The retained triple experiments, 1000-question/10-option evaluation and Tables 1–3 settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds checks of two central assumptions: robustness of the scaling trend to sentence encodings in Figure 1, and structural resemblance of synthetic and real graphs through node-degree and outgoing-relation distributions in Appendix C. The original graph-generation ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 4's 95% regression confidence interval. V3 introduces no repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, significance tests or new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds accuracy, testing-loss and training-loss curves for both sentence representations, extending evidence that overparameterization can impair completion performance. Figures 6–7 add graph-distribution results. The original triple curves, synthetic ablations and R² = 0.85 scaling-law fit remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The logical-rule definitions, training and evaluation equations, and graph-search-entropy derivation are unchanged. V3 adds no theorem, proof or substantive mathematical correction.

C1.justification: V3's introductory contribution summary states that optimal size is solely determined by graph complexity and data size regardless of training steps, dropping v2's explicit sufficient-training qualification there. The body retains that qualification. The prominently restated 0.008-bit-per-parameter claim already appeared in v2.

C2.justification: Section 3 now uses the sentence experiments to explain why removing lexical and syntactic effects yields cleaner trends for quantitative analysis. Section 5.3 strengthens 'likely not directly applicable' to 'not directly applicable' to large text-corpus pretraining; the main memorization explanation remains.

D1.justification: V3 adds a repository link, a reproducibility statement reporting a supplementary reproduction notebook, and a concrete data-processing example in Appendix A. Existing architecture/hyperparameter tables and graph-generation code are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds Albert et al. (1999) on the web's structure, the Qwen3 technical report, and SWE-agent to support existing background arguments. Its positioning relative to scaling-law and implicit-reasoning research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 revises the title, author/header text, abstract and selected introduction/conclusion passages; renames Sections 2–3; and adds a reproducibility section and appendix headings. Most technical exposition and the overall argument structure remain.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a nine-panel comparison with representation labels, revised legends and a completed caption. Figures 5–7 add a processing example and structural distributions. Typography and appendix layout also change, while Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–3 are retained.

improvement.justification: The sentence experiments and graph-distribution checks strengthen support for encoding robustness and synthetic-data relevance, while reproducibility information becomes clearer. These gains are bounded: the main scaling-law evidence is unchanged, full text-corpus pretraining remains untested, and the introduction overstates training-step independence relative to the retained body qualifications.
